card.title: skypod. A Device That Never Existed

details.title: skypod. A Device That Never Existed

blocks.html:
Remember when devices had buttons?

Not "tap here" buttons. Real ones. The kind you clicked with your thumb without looking, because your hand already knew the way. We've traded all of that for touchscreens and voice commands and AI that does things before we even ask. Convenient, sure. But somewhere along the way we lost the fun of fiddling with a machine.

So I built one back.

Meet Skypod — a fully working, fully fake iPod. No touchscreen. No taps. You control the whole thing with your arrow keys and a joystick, just like scrolling through an old click wheel, hunting for the right song at 2am.

Once you're in, SKY OS boots up with a little green glow and a menu that feels straight out of 2007:

  • Camera — because every good gadget needs one
  • Ebook Reader — for when you want to pretend you're offline
  • Games — Snake, Minesweeper, Pixel Racer, all present and correct
  • Music, Photos, Voice Recorder — the classics

Navigate up, down, left, right. Hit OK. That's it. That's the whole interface, and somehow it's more satisfying than anything with a touchscreen has been in years.

One more thing — the background of the site isn't just sitting there. Hover around and it starts telling little stories of its own. Not one I'm handing you, one you find.

It's a small, silly, nostalgic thing I made because I wanted to. Go play with it.

card.title: Chat with my terminal
card.body: An LLM wired straight into my shell — mostly harmless, occasionally chaotic.

blocks.html: A background process watches my shell history and lets me ask questions in plain English — "what was that docker command from last week" — and get back a real, runnable line.
Gave it a system prompt with too much attitude, so it now refuses to help with anything before coffee. Working as intended.
